newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt cuts rice area to save needed water.
newsitem.headline: Egypt cuts rice area to save needed water.

text.p: Egypt, in need of water for an ambitious scheme to reclaim desert land in the south, has decided to cut the area planted with rice this year by about 35 percent, the official in charge said on Sunday.

"The total area planted with rice will fall to 900,000 acres (360,000 hectares) from 1.4 million (560,000 hectares) in the May/September season," Dr Abdel Azim Tantawi, deputy head of the grain research centre, told Reuters.
"But growing new hybrids, with high productivity, will make up for the declining area," he added. The season for traditional types extends from May up to October.
"This will save the country some 1.5 billion cubic meters of water (330 billion gallons)," Tantawi said.
Egypt produces around 3.2 million tonnes of rice a year, of which 2.4 million tonnes are consumed locally, he added.

President Hosni Mubarak last week inaugurated the South Valley Development Project, some 1,000 km (600 miles) south of Cairo, which is supposed to turn 2.3 million acres (920,000 hectares) of desert into arable land.
The project will consume about five billion cubic metres (1,100 billion gallons) of water a year.
Experts forecast Egypt's quota of the Nile water, 55.5 billion cubic metres (12,200 billion gallons) a year, will not be enough to cover all its needs by the next century.
